title: MutCompute guides thermostable Bst DNA polymerase variants
summary: MutCompute predicted substitutions in Bst DNA polymerase; the authors constructed and tested variants in loop-mediated isothermal amplification assays. The Mut235 triple variant showed the highest activity among four tested triple-mutant variants and remained active at 73 °C; its reported melting temperature was 78.1 °C. The evidence is in vitro and does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. The journal article cites a bioRxiv v1 posted 2021-04-15, but that version’s full text was inaccessible in this review; this entry uses the verified journal result and does not claim when the Mut235 result first appeared.
organization: The University of Texas at Austin

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full journal text for MutCompute, LAMP assays, University of Texas affiliation and measured variants; primary bioRxiv v1 endpoint was attempted but blocked, so earlier-version result details remain bounded to what the journal and cited metadata support.

evidence.tested: The authors assayed ML-predicted Bst polymerase substitutions in LAMP/LAMP-OSD reactions. Mut235 showed the highest activity among four triple-mutant variants tested, supported amplification at 73 °C, and had a measured melting temperature of 78.1 °C versus 75.5 °C for parental Bst-LF in the reported thermal-shift assay.
evidence.unknown: The article cites an earlier bioRxiv preprint dated 2021-04-15, but this check did not retrieve its full v1 text; no claim is made that every final-version assay/result was present in v1. Results are in-vitro amplification assays, not clinical diagnostic validation.
evidence.ai_role: MutCompute machine learning predicted amino-acid substitutions in Bst DNA polymerase; the authors constructed and assayed variants including Mut235.
